target_moa.text: XADAGO is an inhibitor of monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B); inhibition of MAO-B blocks catabolism of dopamine, thought to increase dopamine levels and dopaminergic activity in the brain. It has more than 1000-fold selectivity over MAO-A.

citations.quote: The precise mechanism by which XADAGO exerts its effect in Parkinson's disease is unknown. XADAGO is an inhibitor of monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B). Inhibition of MAO-B activity, by blocking the catabolism of dopamine, is thought to result in an increase in dopamine levels and a subsequent increase in dopaminergic activity in the brain.
XADAGO inhibits monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B), with more than 1000-fold selectivity over MAO-A. In clinical studies, complete inhibition (>90%) of MAO-B was measured at doses > 20 mg.

XADAGO tablets contain safinamide, which is a MAO-B inhibitor, as the mesylate salt. Safinamide mesylate is (S)-2-[[4-[(3-fluorophenyl) methoxy]phenyl]methyl]aminopropanamide methanesulfonate (1:1) and its structural formula is below.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence on XADAGO 100 mg/day at least 2% greater than placebo) were dyskinesia, fall, nausea, and insomnia. Dyskinesia incidence was 21% (50 mg/day), 17% (100 mg/day) vs 9% (placebo).

vote.text: No advisory committee meeting was held; safinamide is the third selective MAO-B inhibitor approved in the US (after rasagiline and selegiline) for an identical population, and no safety or effectiveness concerns needed advisory committee input.

citations.quote: An advisory committee meeting was not needed for this application because two drugs of the same class are already approved, and there were no issues that needed input from an advisory committee.

Safinamide is the third selective MAO-B inhibitor approved in the US (after rasagiline and selegiline) for an identical population. No safety or effectiveness concerns needed advisory committee input.

summary.text: XADAGO was approved as a resubmission responding to a March 28, 2016 Complete Response letter (issued over deficiencies in the abuse-potential assessment); those deficiencies were addressed and the drug was recommended for approval as adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson's disease patients experiencing "off" episodes, with no advisory committee meeting held and a single BCRP drug-interaction postmarketing requirement.

citations.quote: The submission under review is a response to a March 28, 2016, Complete Response letter that was issued for a New Drug Application for safinamide, a selective monoamine oxidase type B (MAO-B) inhibitor, initially proposed as add-on therapy to a single dopamine agonist at a stable dose in early stage, [REDACTED] (b) (4) Parkinson's disease (PD) patients, and as add-on therapy to [REDACTED] (b) (4)
Therefore, I recommend approval of safinamide as adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experiencing "off" episodes.
The sponsor should be required to conduct a clinical pharmacology study to evaluate the possibility of a drug-drug interaction between safinamide and BCRP substrates, as a Postmarketing Requirement.
